findings.description: 10 of 300 samples in class 1 show high correlation with the top singular vector (3.3% of the class), indicating a potential backdoor spectral signature.
findings.remediation: Apply spectral signature defense: remove the top singular-vector-correlated samples and retrain. Audit the contributing data sources.

findings.title: Label inconsistencies detected via confident learning
findings.description: 122 of 900 samples (13.6%) have labels that disagree with cross-validated predictions at >= 0.7 confidence.
findings.remediation: Re-label flagged samples using a trusted annotator. Cross-reference with original source imagery.

findings.title: Systematic mislabeling from contributor 'cifar10'
findings.description: Contributor 'cifar10' has 122 label inconsistencies out of 900 samples (13.6%). Dominant flip: class 3 -> 2 (51 times).
findings.remediation: Quarantine all data from contributor 'cifar10'. Investigate whether the systematic pattern is malicious or the result of a labeling tool misconfiguration.

findings.title: Near-duplicate image clusters detected
findings.description: 881 images form 1 near-duplicate clusters (cosine sim >= 0.95).
findings.remediation: Review near-duplicate clusters.  Keep the highest-quality version and remove others to avoid biasing the model.

findings.title: Suspected duplicate flooding by contributor 'cifar10'
findings.description: Contributor 'cifar10' dominates 881 duplicate samples out of 900 total contributions (97.9%), suggesting intentional flooding.
findings.remediation: Audit all submissions from 'cifar10'. Rate-limit future contributions and require diversity checks.

findings.description: 458 sample(s) flagged as OOD: 37 flagged by both detectors, 420 by Mahalanobis only, 1 by Isolation Forest only.
findings.remediation: Inspect flagged samples for relevance to the target domain. Remove confirmed OOD samples. Investigate contributing sources for intentional insertion.

findings.remediation: Audit all data from 'cifar10'. Consider restricting future submissions.

details.pixel_quantisation: PNG export is 8-bit, so re-read pixels are quantised to 1/255. Annotation geometry is exact; pixel features carry the quantisation floor and are reported as such.

supported_attack_classes.description: Pixel-patch, blended, and frequency-domain trigger patterns injected into training images
known_limitations: Clean-label attacks with imperceptible triggers may evade pixel-level detection
WaNet (warping-based) triggers require flow-field analysis which is computationally expensive

supported_attack_classes.description: Deliberate or accidental label changes in training data
known_limitations: Requires sufficient samples per class (min ~50) for reliable detection
May flag genuinely ambiguous samples as mislabeled

supported_attack_classes.description: Coordinated mislabeling from a single contributor/source
known_limitations: Requires contributor/source metadata to attribute patterns
Small-scale mislabeling (<2% of samples) may not reach detection threshold

supported_attack_classes.description: Near-duplicate images flooding the dataset to bias the model
known_limitations: Subtle augmentation variants (rotations, crops) may not cluster as duplicates
Threshold sensitivity: too low catches legitimate similar images, too high misses near-duplicates

supported_attack_classes.description: Out-of-distribution samples inserted into training data
known_limitations: Requires a clean reference distribution for comparison
Borderline OOD samples near the decision boundary are hard to classify

supported_attack_classes.description: Hidden backdoor behavior triggered by specific input patterns
known_limitations: Gradient-free Neural Cleanse optimization is less reliable than gradient-based
Black-box entropy analysis may produce false positives on miscalibrated but clean models
Clean-label backdoors are harder to detect than patch-based triggers

supported_attack_classes.description: Entire model replaced with a different one
known_limitations: First assessment has no baseline for comparison
Fine-tuning creates a new digest but may preserve most behavior

supported_attack_classes.description: Targeted modification of model weights post-training
known_limitations: Cannot distinguish malicious modification from legitimate fine-tuning
Statistical tests have limited power against small, targeted changes

supported_attack_classes.description: Re-submission of old inference records as new
known_limitations: Requires the provenance system to have been active during original inference

supported_attack_classes.description: Post-hoc modification of inference inputs, outputs, or configuration
known_limitations: Cannot detect tampering of records that were never sealed
Floating-point non-determinism may cause false positives in output hash verification across different hardware

supported_attack_classes.description: Replacement of genuine inference outputs with fabricated ones
known_limitations: Same as inference tampering limitations

supported_attack_classes.description: Change in input feature distribution (terrain, season, sensor, illumination)
known_limitations: Requires representative reference distribution baseline
MMD kernel bandwidth sensitive to dimensionality

supported_attack_classes.description: Change in the relationship between features and labels
supported_attack_classes.access_required: reference data with labels + operational data with labels
known_limitations: Requires labeled operational data for concept drift detection
Hard to distinguish from covariate shift without labels

supported_attack_classes.description: Deliberately crafted distribution shift to degrade model performance
known_limitations: Distinction between natural and adversarial shift is probabilistic, not definitive
Sophisticated adversarial shifts that mimic natural patterns may evade detection

unsupported_conditions: Federated learning poisoning attacks (requires access to distributed training process)
Cryptographic key compromise (key management is out of scope)
Adversarial examples at inference time (test-time attacks on individual inputs)
Membership inference attacks (privacy attacks, not integrity)
Model extraction/stealing attacks (IP theft, not integrity)
Supply chain attacks on software dependencies
assumptions: The assurance framework itself runs on trusted hardware
The Python runtime and cryptographic libraries are not compromised
Reference distributions and fingerprints, when provided, are genuine
File system integrity is maintained (files are not modified between hash computation and use)
Clock source for timestamps is not manipulated (relevant for air-gapped timestamp ordering)

limitations: [model_integrity] Neural Cleanse gradient-free optimization may miss clean-label attacks.
[model_integrity] Entropy probe may produce false positives on poorly calibrated (but benign) models.
[model_integrity] Behavioral fingerprinting requires a prior reference; first assessment has no baseline.
[inference_provenance] Asymmetric Ed25519 signatures are available: a sealed record can be verified by a party that does not hold the signing key, which is what non-repudiation requires.
[inference_provenance] Records are produced by a sealing service the pipeline does not control, and the adversary holds write access to the record store but not the signing key.
